title: Screws on a Porch Metal Roof
description: Porch metal in Texas is often screwed through the panel. Those rubber washers dry out in the sun, and each screw hole becomes the next leak.
html:
A porch roof and a house roof can both be called metal and still be different systems. The porch is often exposed-fastener panels: screws you can see, with a rubber washer under each head. That washer is the gasket. Houston sun cooks it. When it cracks, the screw hole is the leak.

What a repair can honestly do

If the panel is still sound and the holes are not wallowed out, the repair is new screws with a larger washer, driven in the right place, and the old holes filled only where a screw will not go back. Screws belong in the flat or on the rib depending on the panel. A crew that “just adds screws” without looking at the pattern makes more holes than it fixes. Missing screws, screws backed out, and washers that have turned to chalk are the checklist.

Oversized holes, rust through the panel, or a porch that was never given underlayment over a solid deck is past a screw swap. Water stains on the beadboard ceiling usually mean this has been going on longer than one storm. We will say if the panels can stay.

Do not put this system on the house

Exposed fasteners are a fair porch and patio detail when someone owns the maintenance. They are a poor main roof. A house wants standing seam: clips, hidden fasteners, a deck underneath. We spelled that out in standing seam on a Houston home. If a bid for the main house shows screw heads in the field of the panel, ask what you are buying.

For the porch you already have, a metal roof repair visit is enough to know whether it is washers or panels. Call (281) 541-0027 or request a free inspection.
